chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Wasil ibn Sulayman, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
'And recite the Quran in a measured recitation' [73:4].

He said: The Commander of the Faithful (blessings of Allah upon him) said: Pronounce it with clarity, and do not rush through it like the rushing of poetry, nor scatter it like the scattering of sand; but rather rouse your hardened hearts, and let not the concern of any of you be reaching the end of the surah.

key_terms.القلوب القاسية: Hardened hearts — hearts that have become spiritually numb and unresponsive to divine guidance
key_terms.تبيان: Tibyan — clarity of expression; making something plain and evident
key_terms.ترتيل: Tartil — slow, distinct, measured Quran recitation; articulating each letter with full clarity and deliberate pace
key_terms.نثر الرمل: Scattering like sand — careless, disjointed articulation with no flow or cohesion
key_terms.هذّ الشعر: Rushing like poetry — rapid, mechanical recitation that loses spiritual engagement

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the proper way to recite the Quran with tartil?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) transmits the interpretation of Quran 73:4 ('recite the Quran with tartil') from Imam Ali (AS). Ali's teaching establishes that proper recitation means clear pronunciation and unhurried delivery — not racing through words like a poem being rattled off, nor scattering syllables carelessly like grains of sand. The spiritual purpose of recitation is to engage and awaken the hardened heart, not to fulfill a mechanical duty of finishing chapters.
word_analysis: rush through it / rattle it off

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali Bin Ma’bad, from Wasil Bin Suleyman, from Abdullah Bin Suleyman who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the Words of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic
[73:4] and recite the Quran as it ought to be recited.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Pronounce it with clarity and do not bunch it like the bunching of the poem, nor scatter it like the scattering of the grains of sand, but shake-up your hard hearts. Not one of you should be concerned of (reaching to) the end of the Chapter (rushing it)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ali ibn Ma’bad from Wasil ibn Sulayman who has said the following: “Once I asked abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) about the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, ‘Read the Holy Quran in a distinct elocution ( tartil ). . . .’ [73:4]

The Imam said, ‘Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) has said, “It is to pronounce clearly and distinctively. Do not rush it like poems or scatter like pebbles but shake up your hard hearts thereby instead of your rushing to finish the chapter.’”
